Constrained Logic Programming's versatility and efficiency are well-established, and this is achieved through the integration of Constraint Propagation with Head-Rewriting in Logic Programming. However with the growing popularity of multi-headed logic programming, the traditional head-rewriting technique is no longer suitable, and a more comprehensive approach is required. Our research aims to address this by developing a multi-head CHR engine, capable of replicating the performance of traditional CHR. Our study reveals that a straightforward implementation of multi-head Head-Rewriting results in decreased efficiency, leading to the development of a revised semantic-driven approach, ultimately demonstrating the equivalence between the two methodologies.

Galaxy rotation direction in the COSMOS survey is found to be significantly more north-east oriented than in the DES dataset. Our analysis of galaxy rotation directions in the DES and COSMOS surveys reveals a notable preference for north-eastward rotation. We examine possible explanations for this discrepancy and establish that it persists down to a magnitude of $z$ of 20.5 in the DES dataset. We have compiled a comprehensive dataset of galaxy rotation directions from 11 sky surveys and analyzed the orientation of galaxy rotations relative to the direction of galaxy alignment. Our analysis suggests that galaxies in the southern hemisphere exhibit a strong preference for westward rotation. Our results indicate that the direction of galaxy rotation is influenced by the large-scale structure of the cosmic web, and that galaxies exhibit a strong preference for rotation directionality that is aligned with their surrounding cosmic environment.

Meta-learning has made significant advancements in few-shot learning, but its performance can be severely impacted by the presence of label noise in real-world scenarios. Moreover, traditional meta-learning algorithms are prone to getting stuck in a local minimum when the outer loop is too slow. This work focuses on developing resilient meta-learning algorithms that can effectively handle label noise and slow learning rates. We introduce a novel meta-learning algorithm called Eigen-Reptile, which utilizes the eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix to sample and propose new learning objectives. By eliminating the need for the full gradient, Eigen-Reptile is able to achieve faster convergence and is less susceptible to getting stuck in a local minimum. We demonstrate the robustness of Eigen-Reptile in various noisy and slow learning environments. Notably, when the outer loop is slow, Eigen-Reptile is able to achieve comparable performance to the full-batch method. We also show that Eigen-Reptile outperforms the state-of-the-art label noise resilience algorithms on real-world datasets.

A major challenge in medical imaging is identifying patterns in different scans that are not easily quantifiable, such as diagnosing multiple sclerosis (MS) lesions in T1-weighted and T2-weighted images. To address this issue, a novel approach called ICAM is presented, which uses feature attribution to provide a detailed explanation of its classification or regression results. ICAM applies the SHAP method, offering a unique, global perspective on each input feature's relative importance. To improve its performance, a feature selection step using Fisher's linear discriminant analysis (FLDA) is incorporated, training multiple models and selecting the most relevant features for each new input scan. ICAM's effectiveness is demonstrated by successfully identifying characteristic MS brain lesions in T1-weighted and T2-weighted MRI images, as well as predicting the number of new lesions in the central brain area of patients with MS.

The current landscape of AI ethics is characterized by a concentration on resolving fundamental questions regarding the ethics of AI, such as what principles it should adhere to and how it can integrate human values. However, this approach is insufficient in providing practical tools for ethics training within AI organizations or meaningful engagement with diverse stakeholders. This paper proposes that AI ethics should focus on addressing a broader range of practical challenges, encompassing not only technical issues but also organizational transformations and increased stakeholder participation. We contend that this can be achieved by adopting a critical perspective on the field of AI ethics and actively engaging with marginalized groups and problem areas.

This paper examines an extension of regular languages called omega-linear
languages, which was first presented in [6]. We are taking a more detailed
approach to omega-linear languages and are providing a detailed analysis of
these languages, including closed classes based on that analysis. We are
identifying the closed classes that can be generated using a subset of the set of operators that are used, including union, intersection, and complementation. We are also investigating the complexity of these classes and are providing a complete description of the complexity of regular languages that belong to each of these classes.

In future wireless networks, cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) technology is anticipated to play a pivotal role. Nevertheless, the effectiveness of mMIMO is significantly impacted by channel fading, necessitating the estimation of channel state information (CSI) for successful communication. The continuous movement of users exacerbates the problem of channel aging, highlighting the need for the development of efficient CSI estimation and forecasting techniques. To address this challenge, we propose a CSI estimation and forecasting framework based on deep learning for mMIMO systems, which involves a two-step process of CSI prediction and forecasting. The CSI prediction layer utilizes a combination of CSI from the preceding and preceding time points, while the forecasting layer predicts CSI for the subsequent time slot using data from the first two time points. The proposed scheme is designed to account for both short-term and long-term CSIs. The performance of the proposed technique is evaluated using a Rayleigh fading channel model, and our results demonstrate the superiority of our approach over conventional CSI estimation methods.

We calculate the electromagnetic corrections for the $V_{ud}$ weak axial gauge coupling by combining lattice-determined effective field theory results with a fixed quark mass scenario. The calculated corrections include an infinite sum of radiative corrections, which we compare to the leading non-perturbative lattice estimate by the MILC Collaboration. We also discuss how our findings affect $V_{ud}$ extraction in neutral pion decays and what this yields in terms of experimental constraints on $g_A$.

We introduce a novel identity-enhanced residual image denoising network that leverages convolutional neural networks to effectively remove noise from images. Our model effectively combines feature extraction and enhancement by incorporating a convolutional encoder-decoder structure with skip connections and a 3x3 kernel decoder to reconstruct clean images. Additionally, we have developed a novel enhancement module that incorporates a 1x1 kernel to boost high-frequency features and maintain image integrity in low-frequency channels. This innovative approach has been rigorously tested and has demonstrated superior performance on various datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results and significantly outperforming existing methods.

This study delves into the general framework of latent correlation-based multiview learning and self-guided methods. The primary objectives are to derive a general framework for ensuring the identifiability of multiview models and to develop a general framework for constructing latent correlation-based multiview models. The research also explores the connections between various multiview models, including their relationships and equivalences. A novel model called the Latent Gaussian-based Multiview Autoencoder has been proposed, which incorporates self-guidance and is capable of learning non-linear, complex representations. The Autoencoder's parameters are constrained within a Gaussian distribution, allowing for a more flexible and robust feature learning model. The LGM-Autoencoder's effectiveness has been evaluated on a series of datasets, including MNIST, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10, in terms of both linear and non-linear interpolation capabilities. The study also examines the impact of various data augmentation techniques on the model's performance.

We've analyzed a subset of galaxies exhibiting unusually red mid-infrared color hues, utilizing data from the WISE and WISE/NEOWISE4 mission. These galaxies, classified as having extremely red near-infrared and mid-infrared colors, share similar properties with a group of galaxies known as dusty ultraluminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs), though they tend to be less luminous. The classification of these galaxies as IR colors-based extreme objects revealed that they predominantly comprise ULIRGs with high dust content. The majority of these galaxies are massive, dusty, ULIRGs with high dust content, emitting the majority of their energy as infrared radiation. The distribution of their star-formation rates is consistent with the dust-temperature relationship, indicating that the observed color hue is a result of dust emission. Humans consistently exhibit contradictory attitudes towards moral principles when considering exceptions, yet current AI methods remain inflexible in the face of complex moral scenarios. In an effort to address this shortcoming, we have developed an innovative approach by utilizing large language models to tackle the "Moral Anomaly Completion" task. This task involves completing partial moral statements with either an affirmative or negative stance, thus enabling us to compare human and model responses. In a comparative analysis with 1,200 human judgments on 600 moral statements, the results indicate that transformer-based models outperform GPT-2 in aligning with human moral judgments, achieving an accuracy rate of 62% compared to GPT-2's 48%. Furthermore, the models are capable of producing responses that align more closely with human moral reasoning, often by incorporating contextual information and individualized moral perspectives.

A valuation domain $A$ can be expressed as the direct limit of a collection of complete intersection rings, which are contained in $A$ and have the same radical. When $A$ is a complete intersection domain of finite type, it is demonstrated that all but one of these rings, which are contained in $A$, are actually complete intersection domains of their own. Furthermore, examples are given to show that this equality does not generally hold, even in specific cases.

This paper conducts a thorough examination of the two-dimensional Dirac equation in the context of quantum field theory, focusing on both self-interacting and interacting scenarios.  An investigation into the one-loop corrections to the mass term and self-interaction vertex is presented.  These calculations are compared to their results in a similar four-dimensional environment, especially regarding the regularization methods used.  Emphasis is placed on addressing several criticisms regarding the validity of the obtained findings, as well as the limitations of defining a four-fermion interaction in a two-dimensional space.  Furthermore, the one-loop self-energy problem is analyzed, focusing on regularizing techniques, the renormalization conditions, and the behavior of the renormalized mass in relation to the renormalized fermion's Compton wavelength.

This study explores the impact of communication breakdowns on cooperative driving systems, specifically in the context of adaptive cruise control and platooning. We introduce a new MPC algorithm that enables the simultaneous optimization of both vehicle dynamics and communication network traffic. By formulating each vehicle's control problem independently, this approach can continue to operate even when vehicles are no longer connected. Additionally, we propose a method to dynamically adjust the setpoints of vehicles in a platoon, taking into account the varying dynamics of network traffic and vehicle performance. Through simulation, we evaluate the effectiveness of this approach in handling communication outages and dynamic network changes, comparing its performance to that of traditional MPC methods that do not consider these factors.

This study assesses Twitter user reliability by capitalizing on the platform's feature that displays content recommendations based on trusted accounts. We hypothesize that users with high credibility on Twitter are not only followed by most users but also share content similar to their followers. We utilize the publicly available Twitter API to gather data on users' followers and recent posts, then employ a hierarchical agglomerative clustering method to a large dataset of users and posts. We compare this approach with two other features inspired by established reliability metrics in the content recommendation domain: users with a large following and a high percentage of users who follow them. We develop a model that predicts users' reliability based on these features and evaluate its performance by classifying users' posts as reliable or suspicious, using the ground-truth labels provided by the platform. We also conduct a user study to assess the users' perceived reliability of their followers and compare it with the model's predictions. Our results show that our approach significantly outperforms the other features in terms of classification performance and user study outcomes, demonstrating its potential to improve users' experience and enhance their trust in Twitter.

In the future, V2X networks will have a crucial role to play in numerous applications, particularly those requiring immediate and precise communication. A novel approach to providing such urgent services involves classifying them as slices of the typical V2X services, which are provided on a regular basis. This paper presents a framework for delivering such urgent services, dubbed $\pi$-ROAD. This framework leverages a combination of critical components, including a real-time monitoring system, a proactive management system, and an optimized transport protocol. A proactive network management system is responsible for identifying network conditions and mapping them to the network topology, while a real-time monitoring system tracks the network traffic flow. This information is then used to optimize the transport protocol, which is a key aspect of the framework. This framework is evaluated using a case study of the Amsterdam traffic management system, where it is used to provide on-demand urgent services, such as traffic control. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework, which is able to adapt to changing network conditions and provide urgent services in a more efficient manner.

Factories are evolving into a collaborative setting, bringing humans and robots together to work side by side. This new partnership necessitates the development of new communication systems to ensure seamless interactions between humans and robots, ultimately leading to enhanced safety. To address this challenge, we've developed a groundbreaking wearable tactile display system, attached to the forearm, to create a new means of communication between humans and robots. This innovative system has been successfully tested in a human-robot collaboration setting, allowing users to convey instructions and warnings to robots through tactile signals. This solution not only streamlines communication between humans and robots, but also significantly reduces the risk of human injury and improves overall workplace safety.

As self-driving cars prepare to enter a shared autonomous driving environment, a range of complex issues arise due to the inherent differences between human and artificial behavior, as well as the conflicting goals of individual safety and social benefits in such situations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a unified approach that combines technical and socio-economic perspectives. It outlines a comprehensive methodology for creating a standardized and efficient framework for decision-making in shared autonomous driving scenarios, including the design of a shared reward system for multiple self-driving vehicles, allowing them to cooperate and adapt to varying road conditions in real-time.

This paper explores the fundamental limits of an online caching system, where machine learning plays a key role in performance enhancement. The key factors that influence the asymptotic performance of this model are identified, and our analysis reveals that a simple greedy strategy achieves the optimal outcome within the context of the repeated linear model. Furthermore, we develop a lower bound on the asymptotic performance of this model and demonstrate that this bound is specific to the particular design of the caching system. The main contributions of this work include deriving a general lower bound on the asymptotic performance of this model and demonstrating that a simple greedy strategy is asymptotically optimal.

Automating the segmentation of medical images has become a crucial requirement for medical diagnosis and treatment. However, current deep learning methods for image segmentation are often slow due to their complex architectures, which hinders their real-time application. To address this issue, we propose a fast and efficient deep network for real-time medical image segmentation. Our approach, called the Trilateral Focus Network (TFN), is a two-stage method that leverages the importance of edges, corners, and regions in image processing. In the first stage, we use a trilateral structure to predict key edges, corners, and regions, which are then combined into a single feature map. In the second stage, we use this feature map to produce the final segmentation mask. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, we conduct experiments on multiple datasets and show that our network achieves comparable or even superior results with significantly reduced inference time.

We present a detailed analysis of the supergeometry underlying eleven-dimensional supergravity by expanding on the Fierz-Pauli approach first introduced by Nilsson. This approach is combined with a novel expansion technique developed by Becchi, Russo, and Storojinski. Applying these methods to the full 4+7-dimensional supergeometry yields a more manageable framework than alternative approaches, such as 10-dimensional N=1 supersymmetry, despite resulting in a similar number of supersymmetry parameters. The work provides a comprehensive overview of the supergeometry, focusing specifically on the eleven-dimensional supergravity superalgebra.

Gradient Boosting decision Trees (GBTs) and their variants have consistently demonstrated high performance in real-world applications, but they are also prone to producing subpar results due to inaccuracies in training data. To address this issue, we present an innovative approach to data quality assessment that builds on the understanding that GBTs update and refine tree structures in each training iteration. By analyzing these updates, our method identifies flawed training data, enabling both data validation and, if necessary, data correction. We have successfully integrated our approach into the LightGBM framework, achieving notable improvements in data quality while maintaining comparable efficiency. Our experiments, conducted across 15 diverse datasets, reveal substantial enhancements in data quality, with up to a 9.0% average improvement in accuracy. Furthermore, our method facilitates the discovery of underlying errors in the underlying dataset.

In this study, we have developed a new equation of motion for qubits that takes into account the effects of quantum Hall states. This approach enables the time-evolution of an arbitrary two-level quantum system to be influenced by the surrounding quantum Hall environment, allowing for the optimal exploitation of external parameters to manage quantum resources. The equation of motion was derived by linking the qubit with a quantum Hall system and applying the Schrödinger equation, resulting in a linear differential equation that governs the evolution of qubits in a specific Hilbert space. The equation was then solved for specific types of quantum Hall states, such as Laughlin states, and the resulting time-evolution of qubits was expressed in terms of complex-valued functions. The equation was also applied to investigate the effects of quantum Hall edges on qubits, demonstrating the potential for efficient quantum computation.

Recent breakthroughs in natural language processing (NLP) are largely attributed to the development of autoencoding models that are pre-trained using large-scale datasets. This approach involves training autoencoding models to compress and decompress text, which enables them to learn representations that are highly effective in downstream tasks. However, the computational cost of training these models has been a major concern, particularly with the increasing size of datasets. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach called METRO, which involves training autoencoding models to process their own output. This approach relies on a signal-based loss function that leverages the similarity between input and output signals. We demonstrate the potential of METRO by showing that it can achieve state-of-the-art results on various NLP tasks, including text classification and question-answering, with significantly lower computational requirements.

Inferring the topology of a complex quantum network relies on analyzing the temporal behavior of its nodes under the influence of external perturbations. Building upon established principles, we have developed a method to extract the network's topology, which can be applied to a wide range of networks, regardless of their size or connectivity. This method yields a unique, deterministic solution when applied to networks without loops, while we have devised a probabilistic approach to address networks with loops. In both cases, we have found that connectivity between nodes can be accurately predicted with high precision, often reaching 99% accuracy. Furthermore, we have conducted experiments on random and structured networks, including Barabasi-Albert and Erdos-Renyi networks, to verify the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

Crowdsourced feedback is a valuable tool for enhancing both the design and the educational applications of visualization. A recent study utilized this approach to gather feedback on a set of visualizations, asking participants to provide a concise description of what each illustration depicted. The study revealed that well-performing descriptions relied on specific visual elements or annotations, utilized domain-specific terminology, and were composed of fewer sentences. A subsequent analysis of the data suggests that machine learning algorithms could leverage these characteristics to create more effective educational materials.

In 1975, Lieb discovered that solid materials made of indistinguishable particles exhibit a distinct energy level gap between the lowest energy state and the next available state, with this difference being dependent on the total number of particles present. This result has significant implications for understanding the thermodynamic properties of such systems, particularly in their ability to store energy. We have found that the same phenomenon also occurs in complex liquids composed of interacting particles. These liquids consist of identical particles that are capable of forming stable bonds with one another, with the strength of these bonds playing a key role in determining the system's energy state. Our research reveals that the presence of a distinct energy gap in these liquids is a direct result of the system's ability to distribute its particles in a way that minimizes energy and maximizes its entropy. Our study of these liquids has led to the development of a theoretical framework that describes their thermodynamic behavior, with the energy gap serving as a critical parameter. Our findings have significant implications for understanding the system's mechanical properties, with the energy gap acting as a key determinant of these properties. Our research has also led to the development of a new method for calculating the energy gap in these systems, with the energy gap itself serving as a key parameter. Our study has also revealed that the system's ability to form stable bonds with the solid walls of its container is a critical factor in determining the system's energy state.

In situations where uncertain outcomes can have different possible distributions, a new method is proposed for analyzing strategies and their effects during a single occurrence of the uncertainty. The analysis is based on a new type of game called counterfactual regulation, which captures the idea that the choice of strategy should not depend on specific details of the uncertainty distribution. The game's value, known as counterfactual value, measures the potential gain or loss that can be achieved by choosing a specific strategy compared to an ideal, uncertainty-independent choice. As a special case, this approach includes the values of other games such as Bayesian strategy cost and regret, and strategy cost. Furthermore, it offers new insights into how changes in the uncertainty distribution affect strategy cost and vice versa.

Urban sound classification has advanced significantly, thanks to the development of sound classification networks, which have achieved high accuracy in identifying sound types. However, a notable issue persists: these models often develop preferences for specific sound types, particularly those that are more common in urban sound datasets, resulting in biased performance. To address this problem, we examine the effectiveness of two strategies for evaluating urban sound classification models and analyze their respective strengths and limitations. We then propose a solution to mitigate the issue of class bias by introducing a straightforward yet effective method to compare and evaluate urban sound classification models. We evaluate our approach using three publicly available datasets, including UrbanSound8K, FreeSound dataset, and Google's SoundClass dataset, and demonstrate its effectiveness in enhancing model fairness by reducing class bias. Additionally, we make our code and pre-trained models publicly available to facilitate further research and comparison.

We have examined the supersymmetric AdS4 black holes that arise in N=3,4-dimensional gauged supergravity theories. These theories, which involve a 3-form gauge field and an electromagnetic gauge field, were found to generate specific black hole solutions with spatial SO(3) × SO(2) rotational symmetry. We identified the N=3,4-dimensional matter-coupled gauged supergravity theories with an electromagnetic gauge field that preserve N=2,4 super-Poincaré supersymmetry in AdS4. We then constructed the corresponding supersymmetric AdS4 black hole solutions in these theories, and found that these black hole solutions possess SO(3) × SO(2) symmetry. We also analyzed the properties of these AdS4 black hole solutions and their asymptotic behavior.

The rapid growth in image data generated by an increasing array of camera sensors on edge devices has led to a significant surge in computational requirements. To address this, sensor processors like the MAX-1A processor offer enhanced performance capabilities by integrating sensor and processing functions. However, their limited instruction set and memory capabilities pose challenges for traditional deep learning frameworks, which are often tailored to general-purpose computing and not suited for resource-constrained sensor processors. To address this, a novel approach called Cain is proposed, which utilizes a custom compiler to generate optimized code for the MAX-1A processor. By automatically generating a custom Kernels specification, Cain reduces the need for manual code creation and complex low-level programming, instead providing a layer of abstraction to simplify development and resource utilization on the sensor processor. This approach is demonstrated through its application in a real-time implementation of a mobile phone camera system using the MAX-1A processor on the Intel MAX-1A FPGA prototype, showcasing its potential to achieve high-performance, low-power image processing in edge devices.

We investigate the impact of global symmetry-breaking on total derivatives in an N=1 Type IIB supergravity theory, particularly in how it affects the scalar and axio-dilaton potentials' behavior. The global symmetry-breaking is linked to the presence of certain topological terms, known as generalized theta-terms, which are responsible for the anomalies in this theory. The breaking of global symmetries through a superconformal transformation allows for the introduction of non-trivial topological terms in the effective action, which can be derived from this transformation. The global symmetry-breaking effects on the scalar and axio-dilaton potentials are also examined through the lens of a deformed superconformal algebra, which introduces a deformed W-algebra.

In high-stakes environments, it's crucial to find strategies that guarantee the best possible outcomes while considering various uncertainties. To tackle this issue, we developed a simulation-based approach to determine the most likely outcomes by leveraging statistical properties of the data. Our method involves using a regression model to estimate how different actions affect the probability of achieving the desired outcome, and then using this information to eliminate regret-based outcomes. By incorporating uncertainty analysis, we can create confidence intervals for the outcome probability. Our method was successfully tested in a simulated medical setting, where we used data from a probabilistic simulator to determine the most likely outcomes.

Aristotle's logical theory, known as modal syllogistic, is a complete and deductive system of reasoning that deals with various modes of inference. It is characterized by its ability to handle premises with both modal and categorical structure, often expressing assumptions about what necessarily, always, necessarily occurs, always occurs, and is true. This logical system is a subject of ongoing research and has been the focus of multiple studies over the centuries, with notable efforts by logicians such as Peter of Spain, William of Ockham, and Constantine Meletios Athonites. Despite its historical significance, a formal framework for modal syllogistic has yet to be developed. This current project aims to create a framework based on modal type theory, a logical system developed by N. Asher and S. Stoner, as an alternative to traditional framework. This study provides a systematic outline of Aristotle's logical theory, with a focus on its natural language basis and rules governing modal syllogisms. It also introduces a modal type theory interpretation of Aristotle's logical theory, with a formal semantics and an analysis of its natural language basis and rules, demonstrating the soundness and completeness of the system relative to its intended meaning.

Quantum causality detection flaws have significant implications for our understanding of causality relationships within quantum systems. We examine the detection flaws in quantum causality and outline potential countermeasures. Firstly, we identify the role of initial correlations in creating quantum causal relationships and the significant impact they have on causality detection. We also investigate the effects of quantum noise and identify a link between the quantum causality chain and the quantum entanglement chain. To mitigate these effects, we propose the use of a feed-forward unitary gate as a countermeasure to enhance the detection capabilities of existing quantum causal networks. These countermeasures have the potential to be experimentally implemented using current quantum technology.

In video coding, allocating bits to video frames in the HEVC/H.265 standard's loop deblocking filter area is a complex optimization problem, requiring balancing the immediate needs of different frames for predictive coding. This paper proposes a novel frame-bit allocation method that treats frame-bit allocation as a sequential decision process, using two learned critics to evaluate the quality of policy decisions and account for the interactive effects of different frames. The first critic focuses on reducing errors in adjacent frames, while the second critic considers long-term consequences of different frames. Our experiments demonstrate that this approach outperforms existing methods in terms of objective video quality metrics, and subjective tests confirm its perceptual superiority.

The formation of planets occurs within a disk made of gas and small particles, called a protoplanetary disk, which is composed of various elements. Observations have shown that the element carbon behaves abnormally within this disk, while the abundance of another element, carbon monoxide, is consistent with expectations. It's believed that the presence of a second, refractory carbon component is responsible for this unusual behavior, which could be made up of particles or larger chunks that are not yet part of the pebbles. By creating a model of a disk that takes into account the presence of these two carbon components, researchers were able to explain why the abundance of carbon monoxide remains the same across different distances from the sun, while the abundance of the other refractory component decreases. It's suggested that the breakdown of these larger chunks is the main reason for this behavior, which could happen when they collide with smaller particles and are absorbed. This idea is supported by a model of a disk that shows that the destruction of these larger chunks is the most efficient way to explain the observations when compared to other possible explanations.

In this study, we explore the application of imitative learning to optimize the selection of cutting planes for Mixed Integer Linear Programs. An extension of Support Vector Machines, imitative learning enables a learner to replicate the actions of an experienced expert, who possesses in-depth knowledge of a specific task. Building upon this concept, we have developed a model that mirrors the expert's behavior in selecting cutting planes for Mixed Integer Linear Programs. The benefits of this approach lie in its ability to identify high-value cut constraints quickly and efficiently, ultimately leading to improved solution times and optimized branch-and-bound node selections. Through comprehensive testing on prominent Mixed Integer Library problems, we have demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach, showcasing its ability to perform competitively against established solvers, including Gurobi and CBC.

In a study, we have thoroughly examined the superconducting properties of the compound Mo$_{0.9}$Ir$_{0.1}$Te$_{2}$, a doped Weyl semimetal, and discovered that it exhibits type-II superconductivity. The superconducting properties of the sample are consistent with the Ginzburg-Landau theory, and our analysis suggests that Mo$_{0.9}$Ir$_{0.1}$Te$_{2}$ has a low value for the Ginzburg-Landau parameter $n_{s}$, indicating it is a clean superconductor. Additionally, we have determined the upper critical magnetic field for Mo$_{0.9}$Ir$_{1}$Te$_{2}$, and our findings suggest that its superconducting behavior is dominated by the electron-phonon interaction.

Effective bug reporting enables developers to efficiently prioritize efforts and address bugs, ultimately contributing to project delivery milestones. However, manual identification of bug attributes such as severity, priority, and categories is a time-consuming process. To streamline this process, we employed natural language processing techniques and machine learning algorithms to automate bug attribute tagging and evaluated them using metrics such as F1-score and AUC. Our research found that certain features like character count and word frequency provided valuable insights, and specific algorithms like multinomial naive Bayes and random forest outperformed others, resulting in an average F1-score of 0.65.

We investigate the anisotropic mean field model for a BPS Abrikosov lattice and a BPS vortex lattice within an anisotropic 2D superconducting environment, which can be represented by an anisotropic graphene structure. The BPS model is a generalization of the mean field model proposed by G. G. Nandor in 2002. The results of our study indicate that the total energy of the anisotropic model is lower than that of the isotropic model near the M and K points in the Brillouin zone. Furthermore, our analysis shows that the anisotropic model deviates from the well-known Dirac equation only slightly, as evidenced by the negligible difference in energies between the M and K points in both models. Additionally, our study demonstrates that the anisotropic model exhibits a first-order phase transition, resulting in a significant jump in energy. However, this phase transition does not lead to the formation of an anisotropic vortex lattice.

In many real-world scenarios, it is often impractical to obtain labeled data for various domains, especially in areas with limited access to them.  Due to this limitation, it is difficult for the supervised NLP methods to perform well across different domains.  Self-supervised learning can be used to overcome the scarcity of labelled data, but it is still challenging to obtain domain-specific knowledge.  In order to overcome this, we propose a new method called Adaptive Teacher Learning (ATL) that uses knowledge distillation to fine-tune domain-specific student models.  Our approach leverages a multi-domain teacher model that has been pre-trained across multiple domains, allowing it to effectively share its knowledge with the student models.  By fine-tuning the teacher with a small set of labeled data from the target domain, the student models can then learn from the teacher using this domain-specific knowledge.  Our proposed method, Adaptive Teacher Learning with Adaptive Fine-tuning (ATL-AFT), also includes a dynamic fine-tuning process that allows the teacher to adaptively adjust the amount of fine-tuning based on the strength of the teacher's knowledge.  By using a diverse ensemble of student models, we demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods, especially in low-resource settings.  Our results show that our approach is robust to different fine-tuning strategies and can be used effectively in cross-domain and cross-language settings.

Every year, international tourism generates trillions of dollars globally.
With an overwhelming amount of social media data and numerous analysis tools
available, the tourism industry can utilize this information to gain insights into
visitors' preferences, enhance their experience, and attract even more tourists.
This paper proposes a framework to extract relevant information about tourist
attractions and activities from Twitter posts, using both supervised and unsupervised
machine learning techniques. We present a methodology for creating a dataset that
identifies tourist-related entities, employs semantic analysis to identify the most
influential words, and employs a Boolean information retrieval system to retrieve
relevant documents. We then apply unsupervised text classification and feature
extraction using semantic analysis to classify Twitter posts, and employ supervised
machine learning to classify both manually and automatically classified posts. We
evaluate the effectiveness of our approach using a dataset focused on New York
City and the tourist experience, and our findings show that unsupervised
classification yields the best results, with an accuracy of 91.7%.

To model the mechanical properties of composite materials with non-uniform microstructures efficiently, these materials are often represented using statistical representations. When a reliable and accurate statistical model of the material's microstructure is available, it can be utilized to calculate the corresponding effective material properties. Conversely, if the material's macroscopic properties are known, the material's microstructure can be inferred. This paper introduces a new statistical approach to create a data-driven model of the material's microstructure, utilizing multivariate function regression to establish a connection between the material's microstructure characteristics and its macroscopic properties. This approach is demonstrated using data from a composite material with unknown microstructure characteristics. By applying a multivariate function regression algorithm, the material's microstructure characteristics are accurately predicted with a high degree of confidence and reliability.

CI Tau is a 2 million-year-old star with a giant protoplanetary disk, containing giant gas voids that may hinder planet formation. A team used the IRIS instrument to observe the star at two distinct wavelengths, and detected a faint signal of a companion at 0.95 $\mu$m, suggesting the presence of a warm object. However, the signal was not detected in the near-infrared or scattered light. A statistical analysis revealed a 3.3 $\sigma$ detection, and the object's mass was estimated to be approximately 7 Jupiter masses, located at approximately 7 au from the star. This analysis suggests that the detection may be consistent with a planet or a companion star, and observations in the K band could further confirm the detection.

We're proposing a groundbreaking space exploration concept, where a self-sustaining spacecraft navigates a stable, off-center orbit around Earth in a circular path. This approach eliminates the need for complex gravitational slingshot maneuvers using planetary bodies. Our design relies on a novel propulsion system, leveraging the principles of quantum electrodynamics, to achieve a high-specific-impulse operation. By integrating this technology with a unique orbit correction method, the spacecraft can reach the center of Earth's orbit around the sun without the need for traditional gravitational slingshot maneuvers. This concept offers a potential solution for interplanetary travel at a significantly lower cost and higher efficiency.

This research investigates the validity and optimal constants of several critical equations and inequalities on compact surfaces. Focusing on Dirichlet and Neumann problems for equations with non-local nonlinear terms, we derive existence results and prove convergence of Sobolev inequalities on closed surfaces. Notably, we establish key improvements in the study of Moore's inequality on closed surfaces, along with analogous outcomes for the non-local version of the Brézis-Nirenberg equation.

We propose a novel Bayesian filtering approach, backward simulation, to track and identify multiple targets moving according to dynamic models that evolve over time. Our method uses a Markov chain to generate samples from the posterior probability of the target states. These samples are then used to estimate key characteristics of the targets, such as their position, orientation, and other relevant features, to predict their future movements. Our algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods in estimating target trajectories, as shown through simulations of tracking multiple non-linear targets.

This study examines the stability of multi-infeed grid-connected converter systems represented by admittance matrices. To analyze stability in admittance matrices, we convert the standard AC power flow equations into a matrix form. We then simplify these equations to two types of admittance matrices, one that involves impedance and the other that involves admittances. We use these simplified matrix forms to calculate the stability margins for grid-connected converters. Specifically, we use the Nyquist stability criteria to calculate the stability margins for individual converters and for the entire system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method using a case study of a power grid with multiple infeed grid-connected converters.

This research investigates the stability and uniqueness of online signature signatures, considering both spurious and missing features. We evaluate the quality of online signature verification systems, measuring both false acceptance rate (FAR) and false rejection rate (FRR). Additionally, our study assesses the range of values for each feature type, the number of features needed for reliable results, and the stability of multi-feature templates composed of multiple types. We also examine the reliability of online signature verification systems, measuring the far rate, hit rate, and overall stability of online signature verification systems, measuring the rate at which systems accurately verify signatures, measure the rate at which systems fail to verify signatures, and the overall stability of online signature verification systems.
In this discussion, two notational representations of the higher-dimensional Hardy sum are explored, along with a brief examination of its ties to Newtonian power sums.

This paper presents an approach for modeling persistent environmental conditions that influence a system's interactions across multiple time points and message exchanges. We apply this concept to autonomous systems operating in dynamic environments, where prevailing conditions can shift over time due to spatial or temporal dependencies. To model these conditions, we introduce a new type of communication channel, inter-process layers, that can be easily integrated into existing protocols, allowing for state sharing and synchronization. We demonstrate the practical application of this concept through an example scenario in robotics, where a stateful communication protocol tracks the system's environment, and the transmitted state is used to adjust the system's behavior through behavioral conditioning.

This study introduces a new neural network model for estimating the three-dimensional pose of a person from a video. The proposed system builds upon our previous work by utilizing a video-based approach that generates a 3D pose for every frame in the video. The current network outperforms our earlier model and state-of-the-art methods by employing a more efficient attention-based architecture. The focus lies in utilizing a standard 2D pose from a single camera to derive the full body pose of the person. The proposed model leverages a neural network with a unique architecture that combines 2D and 3D information to estimate the person's body pose. The proposed model also utilizes a loss function that incorporates 2D and 3D ground truth to optimize the network. The proposed model was evaluated using the CMU MoCap dataset and demonstrated an improvement in mean average precision over our previous model and other baseline methods.

A technique for determining the astronomical X-ray source's energy flux is utilized through the Earth Occultation method, which requires an X-ray detector with a wide field of view. To overcome the limitation imposed by the CZTI's (COS-B X-ray Telescope In-flight calibration) multi-pixel configuration, which restricts its field of view to 576 sq deg, the collimated CZTI setup is proposed as an X-ray all-sky observer. This configuration allows the CZTI to detect X-rays from sources such as the Sun, Crab, Cyg X-1, and Virgo cluster with varying amplitudes, even at different energy bands, which demonstrates its potential for utilizing the occultation method.

The efficiency of blockchain consensus mechanisms can be quantified by their resistance to security breaches and the speed at which valid transactions are validated. Assessing their security and efficiency, respectively, can be done using notions derived from graph theory, known as Byzantine reliability and consensus speed, where the former measures resilience to attacks and the latter the system's ability to withstand them. A key metric in this analysis is the asymptotic efficiency of the blockchain consensus mechanism, which represents the maximum rate at which valid transactions can be processed, even under extremely adverse conditions. In this study, we develop a framework to analyze the asymptotic efficiency of blockchain consensus mechanisms and apply it to several prominent protocols, including PBFT, Clique, and HotStuff. In addition, we demonstrate how our framework can be used to compare the asymptotic efficiency of various consensus mechanisms and validate our theoretical findings with numerical simulations.

In our study, we've calculated the mass spectra of several doubly heavy tetraquark states, specifically those composed of two b or c quarks and u, s or d quarks. Our approach is based on a enhanced chromomagnetic interaction model, which allows us to determine the energies of these tetraquark states relative to their constituent two-meson systems. Our numerical results are in line with previous estimates and provide a framework for comparing the masses of various tetraquark states, including those that can be experimentally verified. Our predictions also suggest that certain tetraquark states may be observable in future experiments, such as those at LHCb and Belle II, which can further test our theoretical understanding of these particles.

We explore the gauge hierarchy problem in the context of the electroweak vacuum's instability. By drawing on the framework established in Phys. Rev. Lett. 116, 231302 (2016), we consider various extensions of the Standard Model, incorporating new scalar fields and gauge groups. The new scalar fields are charged, enabling them to stabilize the electroweak vacuum within a specific range. The presence of these charged fields' boundary terms in the Higgs effective theory then necessitates the introduction of additional, neutral scalars, ultimately yielding a gauge hierarchy in line with the idea of solving the problem through spontaneous symmetry breaking.

This note presents two main contributions. First, it establishes the $q$-Logarithmic Sobolev inequality for Carnot groups by expanding upon the work of Gł\'inski and Nikolay. Second, it generalizes the Talagrand inequality to Carnot groups, building upon the work of Gł\'inski and Guglielli. Furthermore, it extends these results to the $p$-Talagrand inequality.

This work explores the minimization of divergence methods for making statistical inferences. We establish a set of assumptions under which the minimization of an inference problem involving divergence functions leads to a consistent estimator for the parameter of interest. Additionally, we establish conditions under which the minimization problem has a unique solution and a method for determining when multiple solutions arise. The applicability of these results is demonstrated through several examples, including parameter estimation for mixtures of distributions and the construction of confidence sets.

We introduce wildNeRF, a novel approach for generating a comprehensive dynamic scene perspective from a single color video. This method, utilizing a sparse set of RGB-D data points, enables the creation of photorealistic dynamic scenes in full view. By combining this set of data with a volumetric neural renderer, our model learns to identify and connect a network of surface points, ultimately reconstructing a 3D scene layout. By conditioning this network on the dynamic motion within the scene, we achieve a robust and consistent representation of the scene's structure. Our model, fully pre-trained without the need for additional training data, successfully captures the intricate dynamic relationships present in scenes, resulting in a highly realistic visual experience. This innovative method is demonstrated through its ability to produce high-quality animations from a single color video and provides a groundbreaking framework for dynamic scene understanding.

Researchers proposed a quantum version of the Hardy function, which is a spectral statistic for infinite quantum graphs, and found that it's related to a quantum version of the periodic orbits. By studying both classical and quantum properties of the Hardy function, as well as an analogous statistic for a finite graph, it was demonstrated that the Varlamov zeta function can be used to identify the quantum quantum graph counterpart of classical orbits. This is achieved without relying on the classical-to-quantum limit, and instead, utilizes a semi-classical connection. As an example, it was shown that the quantum quantum graph counterpart of a simple periodic orbit in a star graph can be identified and compared with its classical counterpart to determine when quantum focusing occurs.

A novel approach has been developed to identify the interval between two
consecutive maxima of periodic variable stars in their light curves. This
methodology excels over conventional methods, as it leverages the Fourier
transform's phase information, thereby minimizing uncertainties. Furthermore,
it offers more accurate and robust results compared to periodograms and
simple inspection of period-time data. This method has been mathematically
proven to be optimal. It has also been demonstrated through simulations that the
methodology outperforms human visual assessments in terms of accuracy and
precision.

A fundamental concept within Negative Imaginary systems theory involves the Nearest Negative Imaginary Framework (NNIF). The primary contribution of this paper revolves around two innovative methods for determining the NNIF. Firstly, a direct and efficient algorithm is introduced to calculate the NNIF for systems with a limited number of unknown variables. This approach relies on reformulating the NNIF as a constrained quadratic equation and utilizes a specialized numerical method to find the solution. Secondly, a novel method is proposed, which through its application of convex relaxation, enables the NNIF to be computed for systems with an arbitrary number of unknown variables. The proposed techniques are illustrated with the aid of both simple and diverse matrix examples. The findings presented in this paper ultimately facilitate the development of a near-optimal controller for Negative Imaginary systems.

Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems have achieved remarkable success, yet they have limitations in handling continuous operation, where they must adapt to changing acoustic environments. To address this issue, we explore the application of continual learning techniques to improve ASR system performance. Building on prior research that demonstrated the effectiveness of few-shot learning algorithms in adapting to new tasks, we investigate the potential of these algorithms in addressing domain shift in ASR contexts. Through experimentation with daily updates of small datasets, we evaluate the ability of few-shot learning algorithms to enhance ASR system performance. The findings indicate that these algorithms can improve recognition accuracy when the adaptation data are dissimilar from the initial training data.

The task of sentiment analysis in text is becoming increasingly complex due to the involvement of multiple languages and dialects within code-switched language distributions. This study focuses on developing a straightforward deep learning classification system that accurately identifies the sentiment of sentences containing code-switched language. We investigate the effectiveness of incorporating a transformer model into our classifier and present our experimental findings. Ultimately, we compare our results to the established benchmark model from the competition and discuss the advantages and limitations of our proposed approach.

We propose a theoretical model that involves a $Z_3$-symmetric scalar lepton model, 
resulting from the three-loop radiative seesaw mechanism. The model's mass spectrum 
includes three right-handed neutrinos, representing $\nu_{e}$, $\nu_{\mu}$, and 
$\nu_{\tau}$. We also introduce a scalar doublet with a non-zero vev, two $SU(2)_L$-singlet 
scalar leptons, and three $SU(2)_L$-singlet fermions. The model's $Z_3$ symmetry is 
broken by the doublet scalar, producing a massless right-handed neutrino for 
$\nu_{e}$, while the other two right-handed neutrinos create $\tau$ lepton and two 
massive Majorana fermions as dark matter and a mediator. The model's numerical analysis 
satisfies the experimental data of the neutrino mixing matrix elements, while the 
introduced fermions are compatible with the dark matter relic density constraint.

The widespread adoption of machine learning in text-based services has been largely due to the effectiveness of neural networks in language modeling. However, the inherent one-to-many nature of text-based services makes it difficult to accurately infer user intentions, leading to the development of intent prediction as a fundamental task within this domain. Current solutions to intent prediction often rely on rule-based methods that are limited in their ability to adapt to changes in user input. To address this, our research introduces an innovative approach to intent prediction, which utilizes an item-based neural network to analyze user behavior patterns. By leveraging a combination of item-based recommendations and neural network modeling, our approach enables more accurate and robust intent prediction. To further refine our model, we propose an optimization strategy that utilizes item rankings to guide the training of neural networks. Our experimental results demonstrate that this item-based neural network approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in user response prediction, including those developed by major internet companies.

In cell-free networks, user data is transmitted to a central station through a diverse array of access points, each equipped with multiple antennas. By leveraging massive multiple-input multiple-output technology, the signal-to-noise ratio is enhanced. However, massive MIMO's effectiveness is compromised by pilot contamination, a problem that arises when users' pilot signals overlap due to limited pilot sequences. This paper examines a novel approach to mitigate pilot contamination, utilizing intelligent reflecting surfaces to redirect access point received signals away from contaminating users and toward contaminating pilots. In exchange for a minimal energy expenditure, the paper derives an expression for the maximum achievable sum spectral efficiency within this framework. Additionally, the paper provides an analysis of the system's spectral efficiency in the high-power regime, where the spectrum is utilized more efficiently. Furthermore, the paper introduces a robust joint design to optimize an intelligent reflecting surface's time-domain response, thereby minimizing pilot contamination and enhancing overall system performance.

Deep learning-based branch prediction methods have been thoroughly researched and proven to outperform conventional approaches by utilizing branch pattern data to make accurate predictions. However, the evolving nature of applications and pipelines presents a significant challenge to these methods. A separate group of works has focused on developing dynamic branch prediction based on deep learning, but they are often pitted against conventional static methods. This study aims to provide a comprehensive overview of dynamic branch prediction using deep learning, highlighting their benefits, drawbacks, and design constraints. Furthermore, the paper identifies knowledge gaps and suggests potential research directions.

We introduce an innovative framework that enables the integration of a computer-controlled robot with a rotating camera, allowing a virtual object to gather information about its surroundings. By combining an object-oriented approach with deep learning, our framework can efficiently acquire and process visual data. The robot learns to mimic the behavior of an ideal camera, positioning itself to optimize its view of the object's surface, thereby ensuring the highest possible resolution of its acquired data. By simulating an ideal camera, which would maintain a fixed distance from the object and align its view with its surface, we train our robot to replicate the behavior of this hypothetical camera, ensuring that its view of the object will remain optimal at all times.

In the context of a fully packed SOS model with two-dimensional square lattice and inverse temperature, β, we establish a non-linear difference equation tied to the free energy of the model. This equation depends on β and exhibits properties that include monotonicity and bounded values between negative infinity and one.

A new approach to quantum communication has been proposed, which enables photonic links to operate at maximum efficiency at resonance. By leveraging the theory of weak values, an extended version of the quantum input-output model has been formulated to account for the scattering behavior of complex media. The proposed model predicts that coupled optical resonators can achieve a power transfer efficiency of 100% at resonance, even in the presence of losses. Experimentally, this phenomenon can be induced by entangling photons within a photonic waveguide and confining them in separate resonators. As a result, any interaction between the photons will be effectively eliminated, allowing them to maintain their entanglement while resonantly transmitting power. Theoretical analysis suggests that this power transfer process could be achieved with an efficiency of 100% in the absence of losses and a power transfer efficiency of 100% in the absence of losses. The proposed model predicts that such an effect can be induced in a waveguide with an efficiency of 100% in the absence of losses and a power transfer efficiency of 100% in the absence of losses.

We use Monte Carlo simulations and sum rule rules to compute the coupling of charmed and bottom mesons with light vector mesons. Our analysis of the momentum dependence of the resulting coupling constants reveals that certain model parameters have a substantial impact on their values, necessitating careful consideration.
This review provides an overview of the near-term prospects in neutrino physics experiments that will shape the future of the field.

In causal inference, linear regression is often used to handle confounding variables by utilizing a regression model to select control variables. While this approach is effective, it can be flawed due to the lack of transparency in the model, which makes it difficult to determine the weights assigned to the control variables. Our research explores how regression weights influence the causal inference outcome and discovers that the optimal scenario occurs when the causal effect is represented by a linear combination of the treatment and a controlled variable. Our findings suggest that the optimal causal effect can be estimated under this scenario even if the actual controlled variable is replaced with a function of the treatment and the control variable. Furthermore, we establish conditions under which the optimal causal effect can be accurately approximated through regression.

This paper presents a control method for large-scale power electronic devices to stabilize the power grid, using a strategy that does not rely on prior knowledge of system dynamics. The proposed control is divided into two stages: initial stabilization using a network of sensors and estimators, followed by stabilization of oscillations using a network of power electronic devices. A decentralized control mechanism is developed to achieve both stages, which are then evaluated using the MATLAB-PTI-CYME simulation platform and the IEEE 68-bus system.

We are investigating a modified version of the $\dot{u}=-\partial V(u)$ equation where the potential $V$ is defined as $V(u)=\frac{1}{4}u^2^2+\frac{1}{2}u^2\log(u^2+1)+\frac{1}{3}u^3^2+I(u)$. The function $I$ is an even, convex function such that $I(u)\geq C_0u^{2k+2}$ for some $C_0>0$, with $k\in\mathbb{N}$. We consider the equation with initial conditions $u(0)=0$, $\dot{u}(0)=\delta$, where $\delta$ is a small, smooth function. The research shows that the stable internal modes of the equation are those with a frequency of $2\pi\sqrt{k+1}$, and that the stable modes are not present when $k=1$. Furthermore, the research establishes that the equation has a stable kink solution for some range of values of $k$.

The J-PARC hadron program will enable the precise measurement of high-transverse-momentum single-particle and doubly-diffractive jet cross-sections with high statistics, enabling the thorough examination of color transparency. This will be achieved through two key measurements: the measurement of inclusive particle cross-sections with transverse momentum up to 10 GeV, and the investigation of particle cross-sections with transverse momentum up to 20 GeV in doubly-diffractive events. Furthermore, it will be possible to measure high-precision exclusive jet cross-sections with transverse momentum up to 6 GeV. These measurements will offer a comprehensive test of color transparency theories. This program will also contribute to the J-PARC strategy of nuclear and hadron physics and will lay the groundwork for future measurements of high-transverse-momentum particle and jet cross-sections at an electron-ion collider.

Deep learning models can be compromised by the distribution shift that occurs between training and testing stages. To address this issue, we introduce a new approach called Virtual Adversarial Discrete Disturbance (VADD), which introduces discrete perturbations at the individual bit-level of the model's weights during training. Unlike existing methods, our approach disrupts the probabilistic nature of the model, particularly for classification problems with limited data, by introducing a discrete disturbance. To overcome this limitation, we propose a Consistency Training framework that incorporates VADD, which enhances the model's robustness to the distribution shift. The proposed method is evaluated on several tasks and demonstrates improved performance compared to existing methods.

This paper introduces a cutting-edge, model-free polyp detection system for endoscopic video, designed to overcome the challenges of real-time processing. We introduce a novel approach called Multi-frame cooperation (MMCO), which effectively leverages spatial and temporal features across consecutive images. This is achieved through a two-stage process: Firstly, a Temporal Feature Transformation module aggregates features from multiple frames into a single, representative frame. Secondly, a Multi-frame Cooperation Operator utilizes information from an adjacent frame, enhanced by the Temporal Feature Transformation, to refine the initial detection results. We also present a Spatial Feature Transformation module, which utilizes contextual cues to generate a polyp likelihood map, which serves as an additional guidance for the MMCO Operator. We demonstrate the superiority of our method through a comprehensive evaluation on the Colonoscopy Polyp Detection Challenge dataset, outperforming all other model-free approaches while achieving a high accuracy level, comparable to the leading model-based techniques. The accompanying code is available at \url{https://github.com/SHangBoMMX/MCO-SPT}.

A key challenge in wildlife research is understanding how animal populations change over time, but traditional methods have limitations, such as being expensive and only providing information on rare species. To overcome these issues, a new method called Unequal Likelihood Sampling (ULS) was developed. ULS uses a sequential sampling design that weights its sampling frame based on the relative abundance of different species, resulting in improved representation of rare species. By using a unique likelihood function, ULS can estimate the probability of observing animals from different species. The method was tested using simulated data and real data from a stream population of a flycatcher species, and the results showed that ULS was more efficient and reliable than a traditional random sampling method. In particular, ULS was able to estimate the abundance of rare species more accurately, and the abundance of the dominant species' prey more effectively. Overall, the results suggest that ULS is a useful tool for estimating species abundance, but further research is needed to understand its limitations and the trade-offs involved.

The mass of $^{57}$Zn was measured through beta decay that resulted in proton emission, and the findings were compared to calculated values.  A significant discrepancy of 0.51 MeV between the measured value and calculated results suggests that earlier estimates of $^{57}$Zn's mass were incorrect.  This error likely resulted from an overlooked pathway in nuclei that releases protons after beta decay, and the resulting bypass of the previously identified $^{56}$Ni 'hindrance point'.

Ullman has demonstrated that the image of a rational torsion point within a given number field $K$ is confined within specific Galois orbits. These Galois orbits correspond to the image of the torsion points under the 2-torsion quotient map. In this context, we seek to establish an enhanced Manin-Mumford outcome, which indicates that the image of the torsion points, when projected onto a particular projective space, is comprised of finitely many distinct Galois orbits.

The connection between very high-energy gamma-ray radiation and radio pulsars is a key area of investigation in understanding the acceleration and emission of particles in these sources. This study involved a comprehensive search for very high-energy gamma-ray radiation emanating from the vicinity of eight pulsars located in the Northern Hemisphere, utilizing the VERITAS telescope array. Observations were conducted between 2006 and 2015, with specific periods monitored for each pulsar, and our findings indicate no detection of very high-energy gamma-ray radiation exceeding a specific threshold in any of the cases examined. Limits on the gamma-ray flux were established for each pulsar, and these results are discussed in relation to the existing knowledge of gamma-ray emission in these sources.

This study explores the long-term behavior of a specific class of general nonlinear evolution equations with non-local boundary conditions across a broad range of infinite-dimensional Banach spaces. Through a comprehensive decoupling strategy, we develop a robust theory for the long-term behavior of nonlinear equations with boundary conditions, without imposing any significant restrictions on the underlying operator's decay properties or the domain's geometry. Our findings are highly adaptable and provide a foundational framework for the long-term analysis of a wide range of nonlinear equations, including those with nonlinear boundary conditions, without any significant restrictions.

Recent advancements in machine learning have significantly improved the discovery of Ultra-Compact Dwarfs and globular clusters within the universe, enabling researchers to identify previously unknown galactic systems. However, a major obstacle in utilizing these techniques is the limited availability of annotated data, hindering their performance. To address this issue, we have developed a novel approach leveraging Explainable Artificial Intelligence. By utilizing local interpretable model agnostic explanations, our strategy enables the identification of key features that contribute to classification outcomes, ultimately leading to more accurate predictions. Applying this method to a comprehensive dataset of 100,000 photometric sources in the M87/VLA Legacy Survey, we demonstrate its effectiveness in distinguishing between Ultra-Compact Dwarfs and globular clusters, and its potential to significantly enhance the accuracy of machine learning models in analogous photometric surveys.

Recent years have witnessed a tremendous surge in research and commercialization of Suggestion Systems, which are designed to identify the most relevant items for a user's needs. As these systems are often driven by user suggestions, they frequently rely on simulated user preferences to train models. The standard approach to simulating user preferences involves generating random preferences by sampling from past user actions. Despite its simplicity and widespread use, the efficacy of this method has not been thoroughly evaluated. This paper provides an in-depth analysis of the practical implications of using this simulation technique, which reveals its limitations and proposes an alternative method that utilizes sequence-to-sequence models to simulate user preferences. The evaluation of the new technique demonstrates its superiority over the traditional method, which results in improved recommendation accuracy and increased engagement from users in real-world scenarios.

We investigate a statistical testing approach for process yield quality assessment. The process's output is comprised of two types: successful and failed parts. Only the successful parts are measured and their mean is calculated. The tested hypothesis claims the process's average output is within a specific range. We consider scenarios with extremely skewed distributions, which the usual statistical methods cannot handle effectively. A novel statistical approach is proposed, leveraging median absolute deviation, to overcome this limitation. The approach's performance is evaluated through simulations and its robustness is assessed in comparison to traditional methods.

A cutting-edge brain-computer interface (BCI) technology, based on the motor imagination (MI) paradigm, allows users to control devices through electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. However, traditional deep learning methods often face challenges in achieving optimal performance due to their high complexity and limited generalizability. To address this issue, we introduce a novel deep learning approach, centered on the Sinc and Gaussian filters. By combining these filters with a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, we can enhance the MI-based BCI's efficiency and effectiveness. Our proposed method was evaluated using a dataset of MI-related EEG signals, which were pre-processed with the Sinc and Gaussian filters. The results demonstrated that our approach outperforms other established methods, with a notable improvement in classification accuracy.

This is the second paper in a series that explores the CFT data encoding information about AdS_2 states within a noncommutative 2d CFT framework. The key objective of this paper is to expand the existing framework's correspondence rule to cover observables. To accomplish this, we develop the idea of noncommutative $AdS_2$ twist operators, leveraging the existing framework's corresponding 2d twist operators. The article then defines a new correspondence rule that associates noncommutative $AdS_2$ operators with 2d CFT operators and establishes that this relationship is invariant under T-duality transformations. The article concludes by discussing implications of this result, including a proposal for a duality connection between noncommutative 2d CFTs and 2d CFTs.

A computer simulation model based on the UNOS database for the United States reveals that over two thousand potential kidney transplants each year end in the waiting list due to various reasons, with unmatching being the leading cause. Research indicates that many organs could have led to transplants if their weights were adjusted. To address this issue, a two-stage algorithm has been developed to maximize the total number of successful kidney transplants by selectively adjusting the weights of organs that are 90% likely to lead to transplants when added to existing weights. This algorithm has been tested using actual data from the UNOS database and was found to be effective, resulting in up to 15% increase in potential kidney transplants when applied to one year's data.

Sequence prediction is a fundamental challenge in machine learning, with the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) having been a leading solution since the 1960s. Although HMMs are relatively easy to implement and optimize, its key variant, the Hidden Markov Model, exhibits significant limitations in capturing complex data patterns. To address this, researchers have developed a new model that combines the strengths of LSTM and HMM. By merging these two models, this work aims to improve time-series forecasting accuracy. Using real-world datasets, we evaluated the proposed model's effectiveness, which has been shown through experimentation to outperform HMM.

This research examines the boundedness and compactness of the generalized Volterra integral operator in weighted Bergman spaces over the unit ball with variable exponents. We further investigate the Toeplitz operator based on the generalized Volterra integral operator in this context and explore its connection to the commutant of the shift operator.

We demonstrate the effectiveness of machine translation-based sequence retrieval models in enhancing cross-lingual performance in multiple interactive text analysis tasks. We also show that a compact model can achieve comparable results to its larger counterpart, thereby reducing computational time and resource usage. The efficacy of these models is particularly evident in handling text data in non-English languages, such as Spanish, Arabic, and Chinese, which often lack sufficient training data or detailed product-specific guidance. The cross-lingual models have been successfully deployed in production at Qualtrific, yielding notable cost savings and improved accuracy for a range of text-based tasks.

One of the biggest hurdles in data science is locating relevant data. Despite numerous data discovery tools and resources available, the process of finding data is often hindered by users' uncertainty about where to look at first. In light of this, I'll share my own experiences as a data scientist working with government and international clients to access and obtain sensitive data. I'll also highlight the value of developing relationships with data providers and release sources through proactive outreach, as this approach can be just as crucial in locating relevant data as specialized tools.

This study delves into the properties of Jacobian varieties and decomposed Richelot isogenies in the context of hyperelliptic surfaces. It further examines the connection between these objects and Howe curves, yielding novel insights such as a rule governing the Howe curves of decomposed Richelot isogenies, the relationship between Richelot isogenies of Jacobian varieties and Howe curves, and the method for determining the Howe curves of Jacobian varieties via Richelot isogenies.

Recent studies of hot subdwarf stars have identified three new cases with magnetic fields, each exhibiting unique properties. One of these stars displays a strong magnetic field exceeding 100 kilogauss, while another has a weaker field of just 20 kilogauss.
